lessons.title: Leading Indicators You Can Track: PMI, IIP, GST Collections, Credit Growth, and Auto Sales

body.text: Share prices move before economic data, and economic data moves before company earnings. You will almost never catch the exact turn from the data. What a handful of free monthly indicators can do is tell you which way the cycle is heading, and warn you when it is stretched.

children.text: Chapters 2 to 4 showed that cyclical earnings follow the economy and that cyclical stocks anticipate those earnings. This chapter is about reading the economy itself. You do not need a Bloomberg terminal. Five indicators, all published monthly and free, cover most of what matters for Indian cyclicals: the PMI, industrial production, GST collections, bank credit, and vehicle sales. This lesson explains what each measures, when it comes out, which stocks it matters for, and the traps in reading it.

children.text: 1. PMI: The Earliest Monthly Read

markDefs.definition: An index built from survey answers where 50 means no change from the previous month, above 50 means more respondents reported improvement than deterioration, and below 50 means the opposite.

children.text: The Purchasing Managers' Index is a
diffusion index

built from a survey of several hundred Indian companies. It arrives within days of the month ending, weeks before official production data, which is why markets watch it. Two rules for reading it. First, 50 is the dividing line between expansion and contraction. Second, the PMI measures breadth of improvement compared with last month, not the size of output. A PMI of 57 says conditions improved for many firms; it does not say output is 7% higher.

body.caption: Each PMI component is calculated this way; respondents reporting lower count as zero

body.title: Build a Diffusion Index
body.prompt: In a monthly survey, 40% of manufacturers report higher new orders than last month, 45% report no change, and 15% report lower new orders. What is the new orders index?
body.explanation: 40 × 1 + 45 × 0.5 + 15 × 0 = 40 + 22.5 = 62.5. Well above 50, so new orders are improving for a broad set of companies. Notice that the index would be the same whether the 40% saw orders rise 1% or 30%, which is why the PMI measures breadth, not magnitude.

body.title: How the headline manufacturing PMI is built

content.caption: Standard component weights in the headline manufacturing PMI

children.text: New orders carry the biggest weight and tend to lead output, so many analysts watch the new orders sub-index even more closely than the headline. The press release also reports input and output price indices, which give an early read on margin pressure: if input prices are rising faster than the prices companies can charge, cyclical margins are likely to be squeezed.
2. IIP: Hard Production Data, With a Built-In Spectrum

The Index of Industrial Production measures actual output rather than sentiment. Since April 2025, MoSPI releases it on the 28th of the following month, down from about six weeks earlier, with a quick estimate followed by a final estimate. Its most useful feature for this course is the use-based classification, which splits output into categories that map almost directly onto the cyclical to defensive spectrum.

body.caption: IIP use-based categories and what they signal

cells: Late cyclical: tracks the capex cycle

children.text: When capital goods and consumer durables grow much faster than consumer non-durables for several months, the economy is in a cyclical upswing. When durables contract while non-durables hold up, households are cutting postponable purchases, a classic early warning for autos and discretionary stocks.
3. GST Collections: A Broad but Noisy Pulse

Monthly GST collections reflect transactions across almost the entire formal economy, which makes them a useful broad pulse. Read them with three cautions. Collections include the effect of tax rate changes and compliance drives, so a jump is not always real growth. Since July 2024, the government has stopped issuing a detailed monthly press release, and generally discloses the headline gross figure with less breakdown. And like every indicator, GST growth rates are distorted by base effects.
4. Bank Credit Growth: The Fuel for Rate Cyclicals

Loans fund cars, homes, and factory expansions, so credit growth is the fuel gauge for early cyclicals. The RBI publishes aggregate bank credit every fortnight and a sector-wise breakdown every month with a lag, splitting credit into agriculture, industry, services, and personal loans, with further detail for segments like housing, vehicle loans, and NBFCs. Rising credit to industry, especially large companies, is one of the clearer confirmations that a private capex cycle is under way.

body.text: Watch for structural breaks. The merger of HDFC Ltd, a housing finance company, into HDFC Bank took effect in July 2023, and the RBI noted that its data from late July 2023 include the impact of a non-bank merging into a bank. For about a year afterwards, headline year-on-year bank credit growth overstated underlying growth because a large loan book moved into the banking system. The RBI and many analysts published figures excluding the merger for comparison. Always check whether a sudden jump in any indicator has a technical cause.

children.text: 5. Vehicle Sales: The Fastest Consumer Signal

Listed auto makers publish their monthly dispatches on the first day of the following month, making vehicle sales the earliest hard data on consumer demand. Industry bodies add detail during the month: SIAM on wholesale dispatches, and FADA on retail sales to customers based on registrations. As Chapter 2 explained, compare the two. Dispatches running ahead of retail sales for several months means dealer inventory is building, and production cuts often follow. Tractor and two-wheeler sales also offer one of the quickest reads on rural demand.

body.title: Days After the Nifty 50's 23 March 2020 Bottom Until the Worst April Data Was Published

children.text: The Nifty 50 hit its lowest close on 23 March 2020. The most shocking monthly data in India's modern history, zero car sales, a PMI of 27.4, and a 55.5% collapse in industrial production, was all published between five and twelve weeks later, while the market was already rising. Anyone waiting for the data to improve before buying cyclicals would have bought well into the recovery. That is the practical ordering to remember: prices first, indicators second, reported earnings last.

markDefs.definition: A distortion in year-on-year growth rates caused by an unusually high or low figure in the same period of the previous year.

children.text: The 2020 collapse also created the most extreme
base effect

you are likely to see. GST collections for April 2021 were a then-record ₹1,41,384 crore, more than four times April 2020. That 'growth' of about 340% said almost nothing about the economy in 2021 and everything about how low April 2020 had been. For months after any shock, compare with the same month two years earlier, or track month-to-month changes, instead of trusting year-on-year headlines.

body.title: Spot the Base Effect
body.question: A news headline reads: 'Consumer durables output jumps 45% year on year.' You check and see the same month last year was hit by a nationwide transport strike. What should you do before concluding demand is booming?
options: Buy auto and appliance stocks immediately, since 45% is exceptional growth
Compare the latest month with the same month two years ago, and check the month-to-month trend
Ignore IIP data entirely, because it is always unreliable
Assume demand is falling, since high growth always reverses
body.explanation: A depressed base month inflates year-on-year growth. Comparing with a normal period two years back, and checking whether output is rising month to month, shows whether demand is genuinely strong or just recovering from a disrupted base.

body.title: The PMI Dividing Line
body.textWithBlank: A PMI reading above ___ indicates that more surveyed companies reported improving conditions than worsening conditions compared with the previous month.
body.explanation: 50 is the neutral level of a diffusion index. Readings above 50 signal expansion, and readings below 50 signal contraction, relative to the previous month.

body.title: Everything Looks Great
body.scenario: Karthik, a salaried investor, notices that the manufacturing PMI has been above 57 for a year, bank credit is growing in the mid-teens, vehicle retail sales are at record highs, and IIP capital goods output is growing strongly. Steel and cement prices are near multi-year highs. He concludes the economy is booming and plans to move most of his portfolio into metal, cement, and capital goods stocks.
body.prompt: What is Karthik missing about how to use these indicators?
body.modelAnswer: Karthik is reading strong levels as a buy signal, but the indicators describe an economy that is already well into its upswing. Cyclical stocks usually rise most when indicators are improving from weak levels, not when they are at their best. When every indicator is strong at once and commodity prices are near highs, the relevant question is how long it can last and what is already priced in. He should look at the direction of change, such as whether new orders in the PMI are starting to slow or input prices are outpacing output prices; check valuations using Chapter 4's tools, especially mid-cycle margins and P/B; and remember the supply cycle, since strong demand encourages capacity additions that arrive later. Rather than moving most of his portfolio, he should keep a balanced mix and tilt gradually, based on changes in the indicators, not their levels.

body.title: Your Monthly Macro Dashboard
steps: First working day: note listed auto makers' dispatches for cars, two-wheelers, tractors, and commercial vehicles
Early in the month: read the manufacturing PMI, focusing on the new orders index and input versus output prices, then the services PMI
Around the start of the month: note gross GST collections and compare with the same month in the two previous years
During the month: check FADA retail sales against dispatches for signs of dealer inventory building
Regularly: check RBI data on bank credit growth, and the sector-wise breakdown when published
28th: read the IIP, focusing on capital goods, consumer durables, and consumer non-durables
Record each indicator's direction, not just its level, and note whether most indicators agree

body.label: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
body.description: Official releases of the Index of Industrial Production, including the use-based classification, along with CPI inflation and GDP data.

points: Five free monthly indicators cover most of what matters for Indian cyclicals: PMI, IIP, GST collections, bank credit, and vehicle sales
The PMI is a survey-based diffusion index where 50 separates expansion from contraction; it measures breadth, not size
IIP's use-based categories map onto the spectrum: capital goods and durables are cyclical, consumer non-durables defensive
Check for structural breaks such as the HDFC merger in credit data, and for base effects after shocks
In 2020 the Nifty 50 bottomed weeks before the worst data was published: prices move first, indicators second, earnings last
Use indicators for direction and for spotting stretched conditions, and combine them with valuation rather than trading on levels

body.text: Release schedules and data formats described here reflect practice at the time of writing and can change; check the official MoSPI, RBI, Ministry of Finance, S&P Global, SIAM, and FADA publications for current details. Historical figures are as initially reported and may have been revised. Karthik's scenario and the survey exercise are illustrative. This lesson is educational and is not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.
